modules.description: One MongoDB collection with its options, created through `create` and reconciled through `collMod`.
modules.name: collection

absent.description:
Drop the collection. Idempotent through listCollections: one that is not there is a
no-op (changed=false).

★ THIS DESTROYS THE COLLECTION'S DOCUMENTS AND ITS INDEXES. There is no confirmation
parameter — this artifact has none anywhere, and a flag an author always sets is not a
gate. What guards this is a scenario deciding when to run it. No dry-run preview.

database.description: The database the collection lives in. REQUIRED and NOT defaulted to admin: a collection in the admin database is almost never intended, and a default there would create one silently. Creating a collection is also what brings a database into being — MongoDB has no command that creates one.

name.description: The collection this step is about.

password.description: Password of the connection (vault ref; keeper resolves it before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials ONLY — never into a command argument, where `ps` on the host would show it. Masked: does not reach events/logs/errors.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). A value of the wrong type is REFUSED, not coerced: `tls: "true"` written as a string used to read as false and send the password out in the clear (NIM-778/NIM-800).

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate (RootCAs). Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not reach events/errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Defaults to false (verification enabled — default secure).

username.description: MongoDB username the step authenticates as.

present.description:
Create the collection, or bring its MUTABLE options to what is declared.
Idempotent through listCollections: a collection already carrying the declared options
is a no-op (changed=false).

★ THE MUTABLE/IMMUTABLE SPLIT IS THE POINT. validator / validation_level /
validation_action are changed with collMod. capped / size / max / collation /
timeseries / clustered_index CANNOT be changed on a live collection, and a declared
value that differs from the live one is a FAILURE naming the field — not a silent
no-op and not a drop-and-recreate. The only way to apply such a change is to lose the
collection's data, and that is an operator's decision, not a converge step's.

An option that is NOT declared is not compared and not sent: mongod's default applies
on create, the live value survives on a collMod. Creating a collection also creates its
database; Output.database_created says whether this step is what did.
The live KIND must be the one DECLARED: a plain collection where `timeseries` was
declared, a time-series one where it was not, or a VIEW either way, is refused. The
time-series form itself IS managed here — listCollections reports it as
type: "timeseries", and refusing that outright would fail the second apply of a step
that succeeded on the first. No dry-run preview.

capped.description: IMMUTABLE. A capped collection: fixed size, insertion-ordered, oldest documents overwritten. Requires `size`. Cannot be turned on or off on a live collection.

clustered_index.description: IMMUTABLE. Clustered-collection spec, e.g. { key: { _id: 1 }, unique: true }. Fixed at creation.

collation.description: IMMUTABLE. Default collation of the collection, e.g. { locale: "en", strength: 2 }. Fixed at creation.

database.description: The database the collection lives in. REQUIRED and NOT defaulted to admin: a collection in the admin database is almost never intended, and a default there would create one silently. Creating a collection is also what brings a database into being — MongoDB has no command that creates one.

max.description: IMMUTABLE. Maximum number of documents in a capped collection (optional, on top of `size`).

name.description: The collection this step is about.

password.description: Password of the connection (vault ref; keeper resolves it before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials ONLY — never into a command argument, where `ps` on the host would show it. Masked: does not reach events/logs/errors.

size.description: IMMUTABLE. Maximum size in BYTES of a capped collection. Required when `capped` is true.

timeseries.description: IMMUTABLE. Time-series options, e.g. { timeField: "ts", metaField: "meta", granularity: "seconds" }. A time-series collection is a different kind of collection and cannot be converted to or from one.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). A value of the wrong type is REFUSED, not coerced: `tls: "true"` written as a string used to read as false and send the password out in the clear (NIM-778/NIM-800).

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate (RootCAs). Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not reach events/errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Defaults to false (verification enabled — default secure).

username.description: MongoDB username the step authenticates as.

validation_action.description: MUTABLE (collMod). What a validation failure does: error (reject the write) or warn (log it and accept).

validation_level.description: MUTABLE (collMod). Which documents the validator applies to: off, strict or moderate.

validator.description: MUTABLE (collMod). Document validation predicate, e.g. { $jsonSchema: { … } }. Compared against the live one on a canonical form — map keys sorted, numbers by value — so a validator that means the same thing does not report a change on every apply.

Run a raw command against MongoDB via db.runCommand (imperative verb-action).
Defaults to changed=false (probe); the operator is responsible for idempotency.

absent.description:
Drop the database via dropDatabase. Idempotent through listDatabases: one that is not
there is a no-op (changed=false).

★ THIS DESTROYS EVERY COLLECTION, INDEX AND DOCUMENT IN THE DATABASE. There is no
confirmation parameter — this artifact has none anywhere, and a flag an author always
sets is not a gate. What guards this is a scenario deciding when to run it.

admin, local and config are REFUSED: they are what mongod itself runs on, and dropping
one destroys the users, roles and replication bookkeeping the instance needs. That
refusal is the one gate in this artifact that is not just a description, because its
blast radius is the server rather than the operator's data.

There is deliberately no `present` beside this — see the module description.
No dry-run preview.

modules.description: One index on one MongoDB collection, created through createIndexes and reconciled through collMod.
modules.name: index

absent.description:
Drop the index via dropIndexes. Idempotent through listIndexes: an index that is not
there — on a collection that may not be there either — is a no-op (changed=false).

The documents are untouched; what goes is the index, and with it the query plans that
used it. `_id_` is refused. No dry-run preview.

collection.description: The collection the index is on.

database.description: The database the collection lives in.

name.description: The index name — how an index is ADDRESSED, by createIndexes and dropIndexes alike. `_id_` is refused on both actions: mongod creates and maintains that one itself and will not drop it.

password.description: Password of the connection (vault ref; keeper resolves it before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials ONLY — never into a command argument, where `ps` on the host would show it. Masked: does not reach events/logs/errors.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). A value of the wrong type is REFUSED, not coerced: `tls: "true"` written as a string used to read as false and send the password out in the clear (NIM-778/NIM-800).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not reach events/errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Defaults to false (verification enabled — default secure).

username.description: MongoDB username the step authenticates as.

present.description:
Create the index, or change what CAN be changed on a live one.
Idempotent through listIndexes: an index already matching the declaration is a no-op
(changed=false).

★ AN INDEX CANNOT BE MODIFIED. A declared key that differs from the live one, or a
declared unique / sparse / partial_filter_expression / collation that differs,
is a FAILURE naming the field — applying it would
mean dropping the index and rebuilding it, and during that build the queries that
relied on it have no index at all. Drop it deliberately with mongo.index.absent if
that is what was meant.
expire_after_seconds and hidden ARE changed in place, through collMod.

An option that is NOT declared is not compared and not sent. No dry-run preview.

collation.description: IMMUTABLE. Collation of the index, e.g. { locale: "en", strength: 2 }. Compared on the keys you declare only, because mongod stores it with its own defaults filled in.

collection.description: The collection the index is on.

database.description: The database the collection lives in.

expire_after_seconds.description: TTL: seconds a document survives past the date in its indexed field. This is where a TTL belongs — on the INDEX, not on the collection. 0 means expire at the indexed date itself. CHANGEABLE in place (collMod) on an index that ALREADY has a TTL; ADDING one to an index that has none is not an operation mongod offers, so that is refused like any other rebuild.

hidden.description: MUTABLE (collMod). Hide the index from the query planner while keeping it maintained — how an index is tested for removal without paying to rebuild it if the answer is no.

keys.description: The index key, as an ORDERED list of { field, order }. ★ A LIST and not a map, because an index on { user_id: 1, created_at: -1 } is a DIFFERENT index from one on { created_at: -1, user_id: 1 }, and a YAML map reaches a plugin as an unordered structure — declaring the key as a map would build a different index from one run to the next. `field` is the document field path; `order` is 1 (ascending, the default), -1 (descending), or an index type as a string ("2dsphere", "2d", "hashed", …). A value that is neither is REFUSED, not defaulted: an ascending index where a descending one was meant is a query plan nobody notices until it is slow. ★ "text" is REFUSED: mongod stores a text index under a rewritten key ({_fts, _ftsx}, the fields moved to `weights`), so this object could never recognise one as converged — use mongo.command.run { createIndexes: … } for those.

name.description: The index name — how an index is ADDRESSED, by createIndexes and dropIndexes alike. `_id_` is refused on both actions: mongod creates and maintains that one itself and will not drop it.

partial_filter_expression.description: IMMUTABLE. Index only the documents matching this predicate, e.g. { status: { $eq: "active" } }. Cannot be changed on a live index.

password.description: Password of the connection (vault ref; keeper resolves it before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials ONLY — never into a command argument, where `ps` on the host would show it. Masked: does not reach events/logs/errors.

sparse.description: IMMUTABLE. Index only the documents that have the field. Cannot be changed on a live index.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). A value of the wrong type is REFUSED, not coerced: `tls: "true"` written as a string used to read as false and send the password out in the clear (NIM-778/NIM-800).

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate (RootCAs). Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not reach events/errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Defaults to false (verification enabled — default secure).

unique.description: IMMUTABLE. Reject a write that would duplicate the key. Cannot be turned on or off on a live index.

username.description: MongoDB username the step authenticates as.

password.description: MongoDB password (vault ref in operator-input; keeper resolves before Apply). Masked — does not end up in events/logs. Not passed to Ping (goes into the connection).

tls.description: Connect to mongod over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). PILOT: mongo in plain mode — not set.

modules.description: A MongoDB replica set: initiated from scratch, completed to the declared membership, grown, shrunk and reconfigured.
modules.name: replicaset

initiated.description:
Bring the replica set to the declared membership, deciding what to do by ASKING the
instance rather than by being told: replSetGetConfig says NotYetInitialized ->
replSetInitiate; says the set is already exactly this -> no-op (changed=false); says it
holds SOME of the declared members -> add only the missing ones by reconfig, on top of
the LIVE config document, with version+1.

★ ADDITIVE ONLY, and that is the safety property. A member the live config holds and
params.members does not is REFUSED, not dropped (use member-removed) — a silent drop is
how a set loses its majority. An existing member whose attributes differ is REFUSED, not
rewritten (use reconfigured) — a priority change can force an election, and this step
reads as assembly.

★ A mongod started WITHOUT replication.replSetName fails here by name
(NoReplicationEnabled), because the plugin cannot fix a server command line and
initiating such an instance is impossible, not merely pending.

Runs over the LOCALHOST-EXCEPTION when auth is not yet possible: with
security.authorization enabled a set is initiated BEFORE the first admin exists.
Ends by waiting for a PRIMARY; not getting one is a failure. No dry-run preview.

members.description: The members of the set: a map of stable key (SID/name) -> member spec. Keys are SORTED, and that determines the `_id` assigned to each member on a fresh initiate — so the same input yields the same config. Member attributes: `host` (REQUIRED, host:port as the OTHER MEMBERS see it — this is what goes into the replica-set config), `addr` (optional, host:port to DIAL from this host when it differs from `host` — a set whose members address each other on a private network), `priority` (number, default 1; 0 means it can never be elected), `votes` (0 or 1, default 1), `arbiter_only`, `hidden`, `build_indexes` (default true), `secondary_delay_secs`, `tags` (map of string to string). An attribute that is NOT written is not touched: mongod's own default applies on a member being created, and the live value survives on one being changed.

name.description: The replica set name — `_id` of the config, and it must equal the mongod's own replication.replSetName. A LIVE set whose name differs is refused rather than renamed: renaming a replica set is not an operation.

password.description: Password of the connection (vault ref; keeper resolves it before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials ONLY — never into a command argument, where `ps` on the host would show it. Masked: does not reach events/logs/errors.

primary_addr.description: Where to reach the PRIMARY from this host, if its replica-set `host` is not routable here. Default: the host replSetGetStatus names, then the matching `addr` of a declared member. replSetReconfig only runs on the primary, so this is how a set whose members address each other on a private network is managed from outside it.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). A value of the wrong type is REFUSED, not coerced: `tls: "true"` written as a string used to read as false and send the password out in the clear (NIM-778/NIM-800).

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate (RootCAs). Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not reach events/errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Defaults to false (verification enabled — default secure).

username.description: MongoDB username the step authenticates as.

wait_primary_seconds.description: How long to wait for a PRIMARY to be elected, in seconds (default 60; 0 means read once and do not poll). Running out is a FAILURE, not a warning: a replica set without a primary accepts no writes, so reporting the step as reconciled would be false.

member-added.description:
Join ONE member to a formed set (day-2): the live config plus one member, version+1,
sent to the PRIMARY. Not a single existing entry is touched, and no `_id` is reused —
a new member takes max(_id)+1, because handing a new host the identity of an old one
is a way to break a set.
Idempotent: a host already in the config is a no-op (changed=false).
Ends by waiting for a PRIMARY; not getting one is a failure. No dry-run preview.

member.description: The member being joined. Member attributes: `host` (REQUIRED, host:port as the OTHER MEMBERS see it — this is what goes into the replica-set config), `addr` (optional, host:port to DIAL from this host when it differs from `host` — a set whose members address each other on a private network), `priority` (number, default 1; 0 means it can never be elected), `votes` (0 or 1, default 1), `arbiter_only`, `hidden`, `build_indexes` (default true), `secondary_delay_secs`, `tags` (map of string to string). An attribute that is NOT written is not touched: mongod's own default applies on a member being created, and the live value survives on one being changed.

password.description: Password of the connection (vault ref; keeper resolves it before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials ONLY — never into a command argument, where `ps` on the host would show it. Masked: does not reach events/logs/errors.

primary_addr.description: Where to reach the PRIMARY from this host, if its replica-set `host` is not routable here. Default: the host replSetGetStatus names, then the matching `addr` of a declared member. replSetReconfig only runs on the primary, so this is how a set whose members address each other on a private network is managed from outside it.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). A value of the wrong type is REFUSED, not coerced: `tls: "true"` written as a string used to read as false and send the password out in the clear (NIM-778/NIM-800).

wait_primary_seconds.description: How long to wait for a PRIMARY to be elected, in seconds (default 60; 0 means read once and do not poll). Running out is a FAILURE, not a warning: a replica set without a primary accepts no writes, so reporting the step as reconciled would be false.

member-removed.description:
Evict ONE member from a formed set (day-2): the live config minus that member,
version+1, sent to the PRIMARY.
Idempotent: a host the config does not hold is a no-op (changed=false).

★ Two refusals rather than two surprises. Removing the CURRENT PRIMARY by reconfig
forces an election, so it is refused and the operator is told to step it down first
(mongo.command.run with { replSetStepDown: <seconds> }). A removal that would leave no
member with votes > 0 AND priority > 0 is refused, because the result could not elect
a primary and so could not take a write.
No dry-run preview.

reconfigured.description:

separate for that reason: a priority or votes change can force an election and break
writes in flight, and `initiated` refuses this work and names this action instead.

never one rebuilt from params.

(changed=false). A member that is NOT in the set is refused (use member-added).
Ends by waiting for a PRIMARY; not getting one is a failure. No dry-run preview.

modules.description: One user-defined MongoDB role, reconciled through createRole / updateRole / dropRole.
modules.name: role

absent.description:
Remove a user-defined role via dropRole. Idempotent through the same rolesInfo probe:
a role the instance does not have is a no-op (changed=false).

A BUILT-IN name is refused rather than attempted — dropping one would be removing part
of mongod's own authorization model.

★ Users holding the role are NOT touched: mongod removes the role from them, and any
access it granted goes with it. Dropping a role is a privilege change for every account
that held it. No dry-run preview.

database.description: The DB the role lives in (default admin). dropRole runs in this DB's context.

name.description: The role being removed. This is the SUBJECT of the step, not the role of the account it connects as.

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not reach events/errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Defaults to false (verification enabled — default secure).

username.description: MongoDB username the step authenticates as.

present.description:
Reconcile a user-defined role to the declared grant. Reads the LIVE grant first
(rolesInfo with showPrivileges) and branches on the comparison: absent -> createRole;
present and already granting exactly this -> no-op (changed=false); present and
different -> updateRole.

★ updateRole REPLACES the grant rather than adding to it, which is what makes this a
converge: a privilege the role picked up out of band is gone afterwards, and the
declared grant is what remains.

The comparison is on a canonical form — actions sorted and de-duplicated, resources in
one spelling — because mongod returns them in an order of its own and a raw comparison
would report a change on every apply. A role that grants nothing (neither privileges
nor roles) is refused. A BUILT-IN name is refused. No dry-run preview.

database.description: The DB the role lives in — a role name is unique only within one. Defaults to admin, the home of cluster-wide roles. A privilege resource and an inherited role that name no db of their own inherit this one.

name.description: The role being managed. This is the SUBJECT of the step, not the role of the account it connects as. A built-in mongod name (read/readWrite/root/…) is refused: this object manages user-defined roles only.

password.description: Password of the connection (vault ref; keeper resolves it before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials ONLY — never into a command argument, where `ps` on the host would show it. Masked: does not reach events/logs/errors.

privileges.description: What the role grants directly: a list of { resource, actions }. `resource` names EXACTLY ONE of — { db: "appdb", collection: "events" } (collection may be "" for the whole DB; db omitted inherits `database`), { cluster: true }, or { any_resource: true }; naming two is refused rather than resolved, since they grant very different things. `actions` is a non-empty list of mongod action names (find, insert, replSetGetStatus, …), sorted and de-duplicated before comparison. May be empty if `roles` is not.

roles.description: The roles this one INHERITS: a list of { role, db }. db with no value inherits `database`. May be empty if `privileges` is not — but not both: a role that confers nothing is not a state to declare.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). A value of the wrong type is REFUSED, not coerced: `tls: "true"` written as a string used to read as false and send the password out in the clear (NIM-778/NIM-800).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not reach events/errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Defaults to false (verification enabled — default secure).

username.description: MongoDB username the step authenticates as.

modules.description: One MongoDB user of a live mongod, reconciled through createUser / dropUser.
modules.name: user

absent.description:
Remove a MongoDB user via dropUser (go-mongo-driver). Idempotent via usersInfo:
a user the instance does not have is a no-op (changed=false).

The localhost-exception fallback of `present` does NOT apply here: removing a
user requires privileges, so an auth failure is a failure and not a bootstrap.
No dry-run preview.

database.description: The DB the user lives in (default admin). dropUser runs in this DB's context.

name.description: MongoDB username to remove. This is the SUBJECT of the step, not the user to authenticate as (that is `username`).

password.description: Password of the ADMIN CONNECTION under which the user is removed (vault ref, keeper resolves before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials; does not end up in events/logs.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false. PILOT: mongo in plain — not set.

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate. Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_cert). Masked (secret).

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of certificate verification. Defaults to false (default secure).

username.description: ACL username for the AUTH connection (the admin under which the user is removed).

present.description:
Create a MongoDB user via createUser (go-mongo-driver). Idempotent via
usersInfo: a user that already exists is a no-op (changed=false) — changing the
password or roles of an existing user is day-2, out of PILOT scope. ★ the first
admin is created via the localhost-exception (no-auth loopback connection, while
the admin DB is empty). No dry-run preview.

database.description: The DB in which the user is created (login/roles context). Default admin (system users). Roles without an explicit db inherit this DB.

name.description: MongoDB username to create. This is the SUBJECT of the step, not the user to authenticate as (that is `username`).

password.description: Password of the ADMIN CONNECTION (the user is created under username; vault ref, keeper resolves before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials; does not end up in events/logs. ★ This is NOT the password of the user being created (see user_password) — except for bootstrapping the first admin, where the admin creates ITSELF (password serves both roles when user_password is not set).

roles.description: User roles (array of {role, db}). Each element — {role: "readWrite", db: "appdb"}. db with no value inherits database. Must be non-empty (a user without roles is meaningless).

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false. PILOT: mongo in plain — not set.

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate. Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_cert). Masked (secret).

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of certificate verification. Defaults to false (default secure).

user_password.description: Password of the CREATED user (pwd of the createUser document; vault ref, keeper resolves before Apply). Separate from password (admin connection auth): for operator users the connection is under the admin password, while createUser uses this password. Not set → falls back to password (bootstrap of the first admin: the admin creates itself under the same password). Masked.

username.description: ACL username for the AUTH connection (the admin under which the user is created). During bootstrap of the first admin, auth is not yet possible → localhost-exception no-auth.
